description: Estamos trabalhando para desenvolver um jogo de sobrevivência na Lua
summary:
We developed a space mission game that shows, in an accessible, fun, and educational way, how a real mission works. Instead of just observing space, players take an active part in the mission: they manage resources such as food, water, energy, and oxygen; explore and collect materials; build upgrades and new equipment; and face challenges inspired by real situations, such as solar storms and meteor showers, making decisions to survive. Every resource, event, and technology comes with an educational explanation, so children learn science, space exploration, and technology while they play.
Existing solutions focus on immersion and entertainment but offer little depth about how a mission actually works. Our project fills that gap by showing that behind every mission there is planning, science, engineering, and decision-making. This matters because it helps keep alive the dream of children who want to become astronauts and inspires the next generation to ask “What if?”. We built everything at zero direct cost, using only free artificial intelligence tools. We already have a working prototype, and the next steps include new missions, more educational content, and challenges inspired by real NASA missions.
details:
Our project is a space mission game created to spark curiosity about science and space exploration in children and young people. Many children dream of becoming astronauts, but let that dream fade over time. Our challenge was to create an experience that presents a space mission in an accessible, fun, and educational way.

What it does and how it works: instead of just observing space, players take an active part in the mission. They manage resources such as food, water, energy, and oxygen; explore and collect materials; build upgrades and new equipment; and face challenges inspired by real situations, such as solar storms and meteor showers, making decisions to survive. Every resource, event, and technology comes with an educational explanation.

Benefits: existing solutions focus on immersion and entertainment but offer little depth about how a mission actually works. Our game shows that behind every mission there is planning, science, engineering, and decision-making. Children don’t just play: they learn science, space exploration, and technology the whole time.

Intended impact: to inspire the next generation to ask “What if?”, the question that comes before every space mission, and to keep alive the dream of children who once wanted to be astronauts, as Donald Thomas, Benjamin Alvin, and Marcos Pontes did.

Tools used: we developed the entire project at zero direct cost, using only free artificial intelligence tools. We already have a working prototype that demonstrates the core experience and validates the proposal.

Creative aspect: we turned real mission concepts (resource management, engineering, and space events) into game mechanics, and every player decision comes with built-in learning. We also created everything without any financial investment, showing that any team can innovate with the resources it has.

Factors considered by the team: we focused on the early curiosity stage of young audiences, accessibility, the balance between fun and educational content, fidelity to real situations, and zero development cost. As next steps, we plan new missions, more educational content, and challenges inspired by real NASA missions.
